### Outcome & Routine Engine

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `03-001` | Outcome model | ✅ Done | P0 · Desired state, owner, window, verification — not a checklist item |
| `03-002` | Routine model | ✅ Done | P0 · Routine separate from the outcomes it instantiates |
| `03-003` | Monitoring | ✅ Done | P0 · Pure evaluation; normal operation is silent |
| `03-004` | Exception detection | ✅ Done | P0 · Impact and recommended action are NOT NULL by design |
| `03-005` | Replanning | ✅ Done | P0 · Downstream reachability computed, unaffected plans preserved |
| `03-006` | Dependency graph | ✅ Done | P1 · `attachDependencies` turns the household's real dependency edges (the same ones `configuration.ts`'s `canDependOn` validates) into each outcome's own `dependencies`, carrying the upstream outcome's current status, feeding straight into the evaluation and replanning already built for 03-003/03-005 |
| `03-007` | Pattern learning | ✅ Done | P1 · `pattern-learning.ts`: `findTimingPattern` looks at an outcome key's actually-met history and calls a normal timing only when completions cluster tightly enough (consistency ≥0.6, at least 4 samples) — scattered history says nothing. `proposeTimingPattern` turns a found pattern into the same `LearningProposal` shape module 14 uses everywhere (observed, capped confidence, status "learned"), and refuses outright — returns `null`, proposing nothing — once the household has confirmed a fact about that outcome's timing, the goal's own words made a caller-supplied fact so it is testable rather than assumed |
| `03-008` | Optimization | ✅ Done | P2 · `workload.ts`: each member's load in times a week from each outcome's own rhythm (daily 7, weekly 1, monthly ≈0.25; no rhythm set counts as weekly and is reported as assumed); an imbalance is named only when the heaviest carries ≥2× the lightest and ≥5 more a week; `suggestRebalance` only ever proposes the outcome's named backup taking it, within adults or within helpers, never a child, and only a swap that narrows the gap. `acceptRebalance` applies it through the validated, audited responsibility save, idempotent, refusing a suggestion the household has moved on from. Responsibilities shows "Share the load" only when there is something to share; `GET /households/{id}/workload`, `POST .../workload/rebalance` |

WhatsApp becomes an input channel, never an authorization channel (`packages/core/src/whatsapp/`, migration `20261002090000_whatsapp_intake.sql`, applied live). A number is linked to one adult member only through a single-use code: fifteen minutes, SHA-256 hash only, completed atomically by the service-role-only `public.complete_whatsapp_link` from a signature-verified "CONNECT <code>". One number, one member, anywhere. `public.disconnect_whatsapp` keeps history. A linked number's messages are recorded once by WhatsApp's message id and queued (`whatsapp.process` on the job queue, run after the response with `after()`, retried with backoff and dead after five tries). They become `whatsapp` / `whatsapp_media` HomeSend items from that member (`ingestWhatsAppText` / `ingestWhatsAppMedia`: media fetched from Meta's CDN only, type from bytes, private bucket), and a short acknowledgement never echoes an amount, a health detail or a number. An unlinked number is told how to connect, and nothing it sent is kept. Closed-word telemetry lives in `whatsapp_events`. Inert until a deployment sets the WhatsApp credentials |

The classifier reads the whole document into every household-relevant record across its pages (`records[]`: each event, each date of a series, each fee, each thing to buy), each with page, section and quote as evidence, plus pages read/unreadable and the day the document is dated (`issuedOn`). Deterministic backstop per record (no ids, no field a domain does not own); each record's day and time grounded by WonderHome, never the model. `homesend/document.ts` keeps the reading on the understanding (older readings derive records from the headline and needs); `homesend/plan.ts` reconciles every record on its own — create / update (field by field, before → after) / cancel / no change / conflict (a newer record wins, §28) / needs your answer (one question, §29) — with a series of dates read as occurrences, one record on file answering for one thing, a same-amount-same-day bill recognised, and school/class enrichment from the household's records marked as such (§30). Matcher fixes: a part of an occasion (rehearsal, fee, registration) is never the occasion; equal matches ordered by name. Golden scenarios 1–3 (§46–48) are permanent tests |
| `14-018` | Deep document understanding — review, apply and receipt | ✅ Done | P0 · Phases D–E. A document with two or more records is reviewed as its plan in HomeSend and in the HomeTalk paperclip sheet (`_components/home-send-plan.tsx`): Found N items, grouped Updates / New / Already on record / Conflicts / Needs your answer, each row opening to its fields, before → after, household-record enrichment and source page, with per-record include, edit and "who is it for"; "Review and apply (N)". `applyDocumentPlanAction` rebuilds the plan on the server from the stored reading (the browser sends only choices), writes each included record through its domain service (writes moved to the server-only `home-send-writes.ts`), verifies updates by reading them back, records each change with its plan key, field-level before/after and evidence (migration `20261005090000_homesend_document_plan_receipt.sql`, applied live), and keeps the exact plan and receipt on the item. `homesend/apply.ts` makes the receipt: created / updated / cancelled / unchanged / skipped / needs_clarification / failed, partial never reported as done, "Nothing new found. No records changed." as a success; a second apply returns the stored receipt. "Undo all" reverses every change of a document; history names each change. A document with a plan never applies on its own |
| `14-019` | Deep document understanding — HomeTalk attachments & certification | ✅ Done | P0 · Phases F–G. The paperclip in HomeTalk opens the same HomeSend sheet, pipeline, plan and apply — no second parser — and once a plan is applied HomeTalk posts what it did into the conversation from the stored receipt (`documentReceipt` turn, `homesend/talk.ts` `documentReplyText`: "I read the 2-page school notice and found 7 things… Done. Updated: • Annual Day — 12 Oct → 15 Oct …"). "What did the school notice change?" is answered by rules from the receipt and the change rows (`readDocumentChangeQuestion` / `answerDocumentChanges`), never from the model's reading: undone changes are said to be undone, and a question no applied document fits goes on to HomeBrain; not over a voice link, whose content limits the HomeBrain path applies. Golden scenario 4 (same reading → same plan whichever door) in `talk.test.ts`; eval HS-16 (a part of an occasion is not the occasion, 50/50); §50 counts in HomeSend metrics (`documents`: applied, outcomes, changes standing, correct household changes per document). A receipt with a question still open says so ("1 change applied, 1 waiting on your answer") |

| `20-008` | Plan experiments | ✅ Done | P2 · `entitlement_experiments`: one feature changed (on, off, or a different allowance) for a stable hashed share of the households on named plans, applied inside `loadSubscription` so `may`/`consume` and every screen agree and a direct API call cannot bypass it; terms frozen once running and draft → running → stopped only (database trigger); a household reads only a running experiment's terms (column grants), never staff's description; staff create/start/stop through `/platform-admin/experiments` (`subscription.manage`, reason code, `entitlement_experiment_events`) and read per-group household counts and usage — counts only; Settings tells a household plainly when a feature is part of a trial |
| `20-009` | Multi-provider payments backend | ✅ Done | P1 · Razorpay (India) and Stripe (international) behind the one `BillingProvider` port, chosen per checkout by `selectPaymentProvider` (INR or an Indian household → the India provider, anything else → the international one, a preference honoured only where eligible, both defaults deployment config); our own price catalogue in major units (`plan_prices`, readable when active) mapped server-side to provider plans (`payment_provider_plans`, service role only); a ledger of what providers report (`payments` forward-only, `billing_invoices`, `payment_refunds` pending until the provider confirms, `payment_customers`), Admin-read and server-written; the subscription learns provider, interval, currency, amount, cancel-at-period-end and a scheduled downgrade; per-provider webhooks at `/api/v1/billing/webhook/{provider}`, HMAC-verified and applied once; a refund's household comes from our ledger, never the payload. Inert until a person prices the plans and sets a provider's keys |
| `20-010` | Plan, checkout and billing screens | ✅ Done | P1 · Prices decided and seeded (Pro ₹299/month, Max ₹599/month, a year at 20% off: ₹2,870 and ₹5,750); `/settings/plan` shows the current plan with its real terms (renewal date, ends-with-period, payment due), a Monthly/Yearly toggle, every plan's catalogue price with the yearly arithmetic, and "Free during early access" while no plan requires payment — switching stays free until a person marks the plans paid once a provider is live; a checkout summary (`/settings/plan/checkout`: plan, price, includes, region and currency, the provider the router chose and how it takes payment) that says honestly when payments aren't open; a confirmation page that waits for the provider's webhook instead of assuming; billing history with the last payment method (closed word, last four at most) and invoice detail linking to the provider's own copy; cancel at the end of the period, provider first; the landing page shows the same catalogue prices |
| `20-011` | Payment operations | ✅ Done | P2 · A payment that succeeds or fails, and a refund that completes, reaches one Admin (who started the checkout, else the head) as a notification whose source is the ledger row (`billing/notices.ts`, sent from `recordBillingEvent`; stored English only). Staff: `GET /platform-admin/payments` (counts by status, provider and currency, failures, refunds, reconciliation) and `POST /platform-admin/payments/{id}/refund` with a reason code (pending until the provider confirms; the refund row id is the idempotency key; audited `payment.refund_requested`), behind `payments.read`/`payments.refund` (operator, owner). Reconciliation (`billing/reconcile.ts`, nightly in the retention sweep and `POST /platform-admin/payments/reconcile`) reads recent payments back through each provider's `fetchPayment` and records differences in closed words in service-only `billing_reconciliation_runs`/`_findings`; it never corrects the ledger. Inert until a provider is live |

| `21-005` | Health records & HomeSend intake | ✅ Done | P0 · `health_records` (member, `record_type`, `document_date`, `file_path`, `status` active/archived), own privacy-scoped `health-records` storage bucket (object read requires `wh.may_see_health`, not just membership); HomeSend gains a `health_document` intake kind with its own extraction fields (`healthRecordType`/`documentDate`/`subjectMemberName` — a name hint only, never trusted to pick an identity) and its own confirm-form section; `home_send_items` narrowed to sender-only visibility for `health_document` items until routed (every other kind stays shared-inbox); routing copies the file from HomeSend's bucket into the privacy-scoped one; Overview's Recent shows both active and archived records so "bring back" stays reachable, live-verified 2026-09-22 |
| `21-006` | HomeBrain & HomeTalk health context | ✅ Done | P0 · New `health.manage` permission (head/administrator/adult only); 5 new HomeTalk rules recognizing the spec's own example utterances (record an appointment, log/resolve an issue for real; log a vital / set a fitness goal honestly "prepared, not done" — no backing write exists) plus a health-scoped `ask_status` rule ("what health appointments do I have this month?"); `health/domain-agenda.ts`'s `healthAgenda()` joins `gather-assessments.ts`'s fan-out exactly like every other domain; a new `healthSpecialist` proposes `health.notify_overdue` for an overdue checkup only, executed via `ai/executors.ts`'s `notifyOverdueHealth` (needs `run.ts`'s admin client, now passed through `runExecutor`'s new optional 4th param) using the existing `notifications` pipeline; `conversation/brain.ts`'s HomeBrain reads open appointments/issues/due-or-overdue checkups only for a viewer holding `health.manage`, tagged `contentClass: "health"` so an unrelated question never surfaces them and the household's own consent policy (default: none) decides whether a model ever sees them; live-verified 2026-09-22 |
| `21-007` | Vitals & measurement routines | ✅ Done | P1 · `health_measurement_routines` (created first, `cadence_days`/`preferred_time`/`reminder_enabled`/`next_due_on`/`last_completed_on`) and `health_vitals` (`value`/`secondary_value` for a paired reading like blood pressure, free-text `unit`, `status` active/archived, `routine_id` traces a reading back to the routine that produced it), same self-or-guardian RLS shape as every other health entity; `completeRoutine` records the real reading and advances `next_due_on` by the routine's own cadence in one step; `summarizeVitalTrend`/`describeVitalTrend` are pure verifiable arithmetic ("your last N readings were recorded over the past M weeks"), never a stated conclusion; HomeTalk's `log_vital` now actually executes via `createVital` — blood pressure/pulse/steps resolve without an explicit unit (their one conventional unit), every other type requires one or is honestly declined; day-scale reminder sweep (`routine-reminders.ts`) folded into `/platform/retention` alongside appointment/checkup reminders; add/edit/archive/reactivate UI for vitals, add/edit/complete/dismiss/reactivate UI for routines; live QA surfaced and fixed two real gaps — a dismissed routine with no completion history had no path back to "Bring back" (now included in Recent), and HomeTalk only recognized "My X was Y" phrasing (added "Log/Record my X as Y"); live-verified 2026-09-22 |
| `21-008` | Fitness & connected-health scaffolding | ✅ Done | P1 · `health_fitness_goals`/`health_fitness_sessions` (new migration, applied live, verified via direct schema/RLS introspection — no local Supabase credentials available in this session to run `verify:live`'s scripted checks), same self-or-guardian RLS shape as every other health entity; `health/health-provider.ts`'s `HealthProvider` is a real registry — manual/home_talk/home_send/calendar declared `live: true`, apple_health_kit/android_health_connect/wearable `live: false` and refused by `assertHealthProviderLive` before any write; `health/fitness.ts`'s goal (active/dismissed, mirroring measurement routines) and session (active/archived, mirroring vitals) services depend only on that abstraction, never a provider SDK. No leaderboard, no guilt messaging, no child fitness surveillance anywhere in the module — a goal or session lives only in Overview's Recent, never escalated to Needs attention. HomeTalk's `set_fitness_goal` ("I want to walk three times a week") now genuinely executes via `createFitnessGoal`, replacing the "not tracked yet" stub from 21-006; `mapFitnessActivity` maps free speech onto the known activity set or keeps the household's own words. Add/edit/dismiss/reactivate UI for goals and add/edit/archive/reactivate for sessions on `/health`, a session optionally linking to the goal it counts toward. `countSessionsInCurrentPeriod` is pure, verifiable arithmetic, never a scored conclusion. OpenAPI extended with the four new routes |

### Apply with Wonder

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-224` | Simpler apply page: one open step, the rest folded | ✅ Done | Guided steps fold: only "Open the employer's page" is open (one Open button; Copy link removed); "Your details", "Attach your documents" and "Answers" open on tap with a count. The side panel became one folded "Options" row (how much Wonder does, Stop, Download pack, Cancel); the duplicate "Open application" button is gone, "Reconnect helper" shows only when the helper is disconnected, "Stop" only when a helper runs. No change to what any action does. |
| `WJ-226` | Cloud browser: "Wonder fills, you press submit" without the extension | ✅ Done | New service `apps/browser-worker` (Playwright Chromium, Docker/Fly): opens the employer's page in an isolated context, streams it (CDP screencast → WebSocket) into the apply page, relays only the candidate's taps/scrolls/typing, and runs the extension's own `autofill.js` behind a `chrome.runtime` shim — so the form is read, classified and filled through the existing helper routes and `fillGate`, with the session's own bearer token. Used when the extension isn't present (phones). The candidate signs in, solves any CAPTCHA and presses the employer's submit button in the stream; "submitted" is still only their own confirmation. Context (cookies, storage) discarded on close/idle (10 min)/45 min; closed on cancel/confirm/tracked. **Governance:** no new fill path — the plan still comes from `/api/jobs-apply/extension/fill-plan` under the automation policy; the worker never clicks or submits (`worker.test.ts` scans every file but the input relay); only the app can open/fill/end a session (shared secret), only a per-session stream token from an allowed origin can watch/drive it; stream tokens and the shared secret are never stored on the session (only the cloud id + audit entries). Tenant: every app call goes through the session's token mint/`getSession` with the tenant; `cloud.test.ts` covers another tenant, guided, not-started, close. Needs `CLOUD_BROWSER_URL` + `CLOUD_BROWSER_SECRET` on Vercel and the worker deployed (README); otherwise the page says so and offers Guide me. Verified locally end to end against the mock Greenhouse portal from a phone-sized browser with no extension: 6 fields filled, 3 left for the candidate. |
| `WJ-200` | Guided page layout on phones | ✅ Done | The employer's address wrapped one letter per line beside the buttons: now the address is one shortened line (host + path) with Open page / Copy link full-width beneath; stepper labels wrap instead of truncating. |
| `WJ-201` | Guided application made useful | ✅ Done | Four steps: open the page; your details (tap a row to copy — no button per row); documents; answers the form may ask for. Only real answers are offered: remembered answers first (notice period, expected salary…), then AI drafts that say something (labelled "AI draft, in your words" or "check the facts"); a draft that was only "[Add your notice period…]" is no longer shown as an answer — it becomes a field the candidate answers once and Wonder remembers (`memoryKeyFor`), and work authorization / sponsorship stay on the form. Nothing submits; "Did you submit?" is unchanged. Tests: `classify.test.ts`. |

| `WJ-220` | Show the site an Adzuna job lives on, resolved once and shared | ✅ Done | Adzuna's API has no source field, only its own link. The link check (which already follows each visible job's link to see if it's still open) now records where an Adzuna link lands ("naukri.com") — no extra request — in `wonderjobs.job_origins`, keyed by Adzuna's ad id. Every later check, for any candidate, uses the stored site instead of following Adzuna's link again (and checks that site directly). Cards read "naukri.com via Adzuna India"; the job page "On naukri.com, via Adzuna India". Nothing is shown when the link stays on Adzuna or can't be followed. **Governance:** `job_origins` is intentionally not tenant-scoped — it holds only public facts about public postings (ad id, landing host/URL, time), nothing about who viewed them; RLS on, anon/authenticated revoked, service role only. Writes come only from the server's own follow, never from client input. Migration 0012 applied to production. |

| `WJ-021` | Scheduled runs | ✅ Done | List, enable/disable, run now, duplicate, delete. Due schedules now actually fire while the app is open via `services/scheduler.ts` (`SchedulerRunner`, one tick per minute, idempotent: the schedule advances before the run starts). |
| `WJ-022` | Scheduled workflow builder | ✅ Done | `ScheduleBuilder` — trigger/schedule/stages/search/conditions/actions/level/provider. |
| `WJ-023` | Workflow templates | ✅ Done | `services/mock/templates.ts` — 5 templates, duplicate supported. |
| `WJ-024` | Silence/no-op outcome | ✅ Done | Each schedule's condition (`strong_matches > n`, `new_jobs > n`, `always`) is carried on the run and evaluated by `conditionMet()` in the engine (unit tested); unmet → `silent`, no notification; cards say "quiet — nothing to report". |
| `WJ-094` | Server-side cron for scheduled runs | ✅ Done | `GET /api/cron/scheduled-runs` (Vercel Cron, `vercel.json`; `CRON_SECRET` bearer, 503 without one) fires every tenant's due schedules with nobody's tab open. `server/workflow/dueTenants.ts` asks the database which tenants have work (`wonderjobs.due_schedule_tenants`, migration `0004`) instead of pulling every workflow document; `server/workflow/snapshot.ts` loads a tenant's career/jobs/workflow/automation documents in the client's own persisted shape (`server/clientState.ts`) and writes them back with the same trimming the browser's `partialize` applies; `server/workflow/serverExecutors.ts` runs profile → search → dedupe → understand → match → quality → rank through the **same** `WorkflowEngine` the browser uses, against `server/jobs/search.ts`. Stages needing the candidate (prepare, review, apply) are deliberately not run — the shortlist, saved jobs and a notification are waiting when they next sign in. Idempotent by construction: the schedule's `nextRunAt` advances *before* the run starts, so a crash or a timeout can never re-fire in a loop; one run per tenant per tick, skipped while another run is active; per-tenant 60 s and per-invocation 240 s budgets. Schedule times are now evaluated in the schedule's own timezone (`domain/workflow/schedule.ts`, DST-aware, 8 unit tests) — the old `setHours` version would have moved everyone's 08:00 to 08:00 UTC once the cron owned it; the browser uses the same function. Cadence is a deployment fact, not an assumption: Vercel's Hobby plan runs a cron **once a day** (a `*/15` schedule fails the build there), which is a safety net rather than a scheduler, so `vercel.json` ships `0 2 * * *` and the browser keeps firing schedules at their proper time. `CRON_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 1440) declares the real cadence; at or below 60 the cron owns scheduling and the client ticker stands down (`server/workflow/cronCadence.ts`, reported to the browser by `/api/jobs/sources`). They can never double-fire either way: one `isDue` rule — shared by the browser, the cron and the SQL — skips a schedule that already ran in the last 12 hours, which is shorter than the gap between any two legitimate firings this product can express. 7 unit tests cover firing, publishing the catalog, notifying, staying silent when the condition isn't met, advancing on failure, skipping review-only schedules and refusing to start a second concurrent run. |
| `WJ-097` | Follow-up and interview reminders from the server | ✅ Done | The cron's second pass (`server/workflow/reminders.ts`, same `/api/cron/scheduled-runs` invocation) raises the reminders the browser's ticker used to raise only while a tab was open — an interview on Tuesday is exactly what someone needs told to them on Monday. Tenants with something near enough to matter come from `wonderjobs.due_reminder_tenants` (migration `0006`, a jsonb query over applications' follow-ups) instead of reading every tenant's applications. Lead times match the browser's: two days for an interview, one for a follow-up, and still worth saying for a day after it was due. Idempotent through the **same** `career.reminded` list the browser writes, so the two can never raise the same reminder twice, and the career document is merged rather than replaced so a concurrent tab doesn't lose work. Each reminder is also pushed (WJ-096). Reminders run even when the schedule pass has eaten most of the invocation's budget: a missed interview reminder is worse than a late run. 10 unit tests. |

The debounce is flushed on unmount so switching tabs (the parent already remounts per tab via `key={tab}`) never drops the last <800ms of typing. A small "Saving…"/"Saved" status replaces the old explicit Save button. The read-only version-compare view renders through the same `markdownToHtml`, so it's no longer raw text there either. 9 new unit tests for the markdown↔HTML conversion, including a full round-trip through a realistic resume. Verified live end to end in the browser (Playwright): typed edits render richly formatted immediately, the provenance badge flips to "User-modified" and the version count stays at 1 (no version created), the edit survives a tab-away-and-back, the Bold toolbar button works, and the actual persisted store content is confirmed to be real markdown (`**bold me**`), not HTML. `npm run check` green (238/238, full production build). |
| `WJ-119` | Download the current resume/cover letter as a real .docx from the application page | ✅ Done | `lib/zip.ts`: a minimal, dependency-free, isomorphic ZIP writer (STORED entries, so no `node:zlib`, works identically in the browser and Node) with a hand-rolled CRC-32 — round-trips through `server/resume/extractText.ts`'s existing DOCX *reader* (exported `readZipEntries`/`readZipEntry` for this), and the CRC implementation is checked against the standard IEEE 802.3 test vector (`crc32("123456789") === 0xCBF43926`). `lib/richtext.ts` gained `parseMarkdownBlocks`, the same markdown grammar `markdownToHtml` renders but as structured blocks/runs instead of HTML — one parser, so a downloaded file can never drift from what the rich-text editor shows on screen. `lib/docx.ts` turns those blocks into real Office Open XML (`word/document.xml` + `styles.xml` for heading/list styles + `numbering.xml` for real bullet-list numbering + the package/content-type boilerplate a valid .docx needs) and zips them up — entirely client-side, no server round trip, since the content is already in the browser's own state. The application detail page (`/app/applications/[id]`) shows "Download resume (.docx)" / "Download cover letter (.docx)" above "Submit on \<company\>'s site", one per artifact that actually exists (never a button for a document that wasn't generated), downloading via an in-memory `Blob` (`lib/download.ts`) with a sanitized `\<Company\>-Resume.docx` filename — no dependency, `docx` npm package or otherwise. Verification went well beyond this repo's own reader: LibreOffice's headless converter turned out to be broken in this sandbox for *any* input file including a plain .txt, so real validation used `python-docx` (an independent, spec-strict OOXML library, installed fresh for this) to open generated files — it resolved the custom heading/list styles correctly and read back every heading, bold run, italic run and bullet exactly as written. Confirmed live end to end: clicked both real download buttons in a running browser, saved the actual downloaded files, and opened them with `python-docx` — correct structure and content in both. 9 new unit tests (`zip.test.ts`, `docx.test.ts`) covering the CRC vector, a full DOCX-reader round-trip, XML escaping (a title containing `<`/`&`/`"` never produces invalid XML), and the required OOXML parts being present. `npm run check` green (251/251, full production build). |

The CV's exporter wraps a spacer glyph after each bullet in marked content `/Span<</ActualText <FEFF200B> >> BDC … EMC` (ActualText = byte-order mark + zero-width space, i.e. "this reads as nothing"). `extractText.readContentStream` matched every `(…)`/`<…>` as drawn text, so it picked up the ActualText value, decoded it one byte at a time as Latin-1 (FE FF → "þÿ"), and also kept the spacer glyph (shown as "("). Fixed at the root: `/ActualText` is now read as a PDF *text string* (`decodeTextString`: UTF-16BE after FE FF, UTF-8 after EF BB BF, else bytes) and, per the PDF spec, replaces the glyphs of its `BDC … EMC` span (nesting tracked; `BMC` and spans without ActualText unchanged); a hex string that starts with FE FF is decoded as UTF-16 too; `tidy()` drops byte-order marks, zero-width characters and control characters. On the reported CV: 0 stray characters, all 10 roles, bullets start with their text. Production check: no saved Career Profile contains these characters (the import shown had not been saved), so no data repair was needed. Tests in `extractText.test.ts` (zero-width ActualText span, UTF-16/byte ActualText replacing glyphs, marked content without ActualText untouched, text-string decoding). |

Pass = full points, warn = half, fail = 0; checks that don't apply (e.g. Word-only checks on a PDF) leave the score; an unreadable/scanned file scores 0. Each finding has severity (Fix first / Improve / Tip), the résumé's own text as evidence and a fix pointing to the Career Profile, the builder or the file. **File signals** (`server/resume/fileSignals.ts`): PDF page count, images, Type0 fonts without ToUnicode, link targets, and **column detection** from line-start positions (follows `q/Q/cm/BT/Tm/Td/TD/T*`; many prose lines starting at one point mid-page = columns; right-aligned dates, centred headings and skill grids don't count); DOCX tables, text boxes, `w:cols`, header/footer text, media, hyperlinks, page count. **API**: `POST /api/resume-files/[id]/ats` (own file only, tenant-filtered, rate-limited, nothing stored). **Reader improvements found by running our own 8 templates through it** (also improve import): Word list paragraphs keep a "•" mark; a lone bullet mark line starts an achievement and unmarked lines continue it; role headers accept "Pvt. ### Reliability

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-161` | Two production defects found by the walk-through | ✅ Done | (1) JobsLake gave two different postings the same id when one source listed the same title, employer and place twice; the warm-pool upsert then failed (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time`) and the whole search failed, so WonderJobs fell back to searching sources directly. Colliding postings now get an id from their own source record (stable across searches), and run-history/warm-pool writes are bookkeeping — a failed write is logged for operators, never a failed search; the stream route now logs the exception it used to swallow. (2) Sync race: the page-start `GET /api/state` could answer after a write made on that page had already been pushed and un-dirtied, and its older copy replaced the newer local state (seen as a just-saved résumé disappearing, which also disables Apply with Wonder). Stores changed on the page now keep their local copy during that revalidation. Tests: `jobslake.test.ts`, `core.test.ts`, `remoteStorage.test.ts` (each failed before the fix). No governance change: no new capability, AI path or external action. |

### Auth / Persistence

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |

| `WJ-146` | Real Supabase run of `auth.spec.ts` surfaced a genuine account-continuity bug: a just-completed onboarding could be lost on sign-out | ✅ Done | `signOutEverywhere()` (`lib/auth/browser.ts`) wipes this account's local storage and revokes its session immediately; store writes are debounced (`store/remoteStorage.ts`, SERIALIZE_MS + PUSH_MS) and `flushRemote()` was fire-and-forget (`void pushNow(...)`), so a write still inside that window at sign-out time (e.g. `completeOnboarding()`, right before the AUTH-007 flow signs out) never reached the server and was gone once local storage was cleared. `flushRemote()` now returns the request; `TopBar` and `/app/profile`'s sign-out handlers `await flushRemote(false)` before `signOutEverywhere()`. Unit test asserts the returned promise only resolves once the write lands. **Verified against the real project**: created disposable, pre-confirmed test accounts via the admin API (no real email sent), ran the full account-dependent block of `auth.spec.ts` end to end, deleted each account and its rows afterward — 13/13 runnable tests pass (5 remain the suite's own documented skips: real email, OAuth, clock control). **Governance:** no auth/session/tenant logic changed — only when a write is flushed relative to sign-out; nothing here touches `resolveCapability` or any gated action. |

| `WJ-132` | UX Simplification Phase 3.1 + 3.3 — Ask Wonder real natural-language-to-action interface | ✅ Done | "Ask Wonder anything…" (the global command field) was a command palette that only fuzzy-matched page names and treated everything else as a job search, despite the "anything" framing implying real natural-language understanding. `domain/wonder/intent.ts` adds a deterministic pattern-based intent router (no model call, no free-text reply, no hidden reasoning — not a chatbot) for a fixed set of real actions; `domain/wonder/resolve.ts` resolves a matched intent against the candidate's own live data (jobs, matches, applications, Career DNA) into one concrete action, returning `null` for anything it can't back with real data so `CommandPalette` falls through to its existing plain-job-search default. Recognized: "what applications need my attention" (reuses `computeApplicationAttention`, the same function Home/Applications already use, so the count can't disagree with what's shown there); "what skills am I missing" (`domain/wonder/insights.ts::computeMissingSkills` — a real aggregation of skills the candidate's own strong/worth-considering matches ask for that aren't in their Career DNA, never a canned "learn X" list); "improve my linkedin headline" (routes to Career Profile's headline field with an explicit "LinkedIn isn't connected" disclosure rather than fabricating a LinkedIn feature); natural-language scheduling, e.g. "search for backend engineer roles weekly" (picks the closest existing `SCHEDULE_TEMPLATES` entry by the frequency word used and hands the candidate's own search text to `/app/automation/scheduled/new?q=...` as a real, editable starting value — nothing is scheduled until the candidate reviews and confirms the builder themselves, preserving the "AI proposes, application code decides" rule); "why isn't the Stripe job showing" (`domain/jobs/filterExplain.ts` gained `explainJobVisibility`, refactored to share one `firstFailedReason` helper with `applyJobFilters` so a single-job explanation and the results list's aggregate breakdown can never disagree about why something is hidden — distinguishes "not in your catalog at all" from "hidden by an active filter" and names the specific filter); "prepare an application for Stripe" (real catalog lookup via `domain/wonder/insights.ts::findJobBySubject`, opens the job's page if found, returns nothing rather than fabricating a match otherwise). 29 new unit tests (`intent.test.ts`, `insights.test.ts`, `resolve.test.ts`, plus 4 added to `filterExplain.test.ts`) — 336 total, all passing. Verified end-to-end in a browser via Playwright: all 5 intents resolve correctly against real demo data with no console errors; the scheduling flow was driven through to the New Scheduled Run form, confirming the real derived search text appears in the editable Search query field before anything is created. `npm run check` (lint/typecheck/336 tests/production build) green. |

Both call sites now dispatch through `getServerProvider(platform.provider)`. `GET /api/ai/keys` and the AI store expose which vendor is running so the settings page and privacy page no longer claim “Anthropic” unconditionally. 11 unit tests covering vendor selection, both fallback chains, the invalid-value default, case/whitespace handling and the model override; `npm run check` 169/169. |

All three adapters now read/pass the vendor's real error text. Couldn't inspect this deployment's actual Vercel env vars or logs (outside this session's connected accounts) to confirm the exact misconfiguration — most likely `WONDERJOBS_AI_MODEL` is set to a name Gemini doesn't recognize, or the key isn't a Generative Language API (AI Studio) key; the next occurrence will now say which. 4 new unit tests (`server/providers/types.test.ts`). `npm run check` 193/193. |

Confirmed against the live deployment (`wonder-team4/wonderjobs` on Vercel): `WONDERJOBS_AI_PROVIDER=gemini` is set, no `WONDERJOBS_AI_MODEL` override, so the code's hardcoded default was the only thing that could be stale. `platform.ts`'s `DEFAULT_MODEL.gemini` updated from `gemini-2.5-flash` to `gemini-3.6-flash` (the exact model Google's own error told us to use), and the BYOK Gemini model picker (`domain/ai/types.ts`) swapped the same deprecated option for it — `gemini-2.5-pro` (still the BYOK default) left untouched since nothing confirmed it's also deprecated and changing it without evidence would've been a guess. `npm run check` 193/193. |

Subscriptions live in `wonderjobs.push_subscriptions` (migration `0005`), one row per browser; a 404/410 from a push service means the browser dropped the subscription, so the row is deleted rather than retried forever. `POST/GET/DELETE /api/push/subscribe` (session required, rate-limited, tenant-scoped delete so no account can unsubscribe another's browser); the POST sends a real notification straight away so "it's on" is something the candidate sees. `components/pwa/PushNotifications.tsx` on the Profile page never asks for permission on load — an uninvited prompt is how a site gets blocked permanently, and a blocked browser can't be un-blocked from the page — and the whole card is hidden on deployments with no keys. `public/sw.js` gained `push` and `notificationclick` handlers, the latter reusing an open tab instead of opening a window per notification. Wired into the scheduled-run cron: the in-app notification is saved first and is the record; the push is sent last and can never cost a run its results. Operator setup is `npm run push:keys` plus three environment variables. 17 unit tests. |

### Career DNA

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-095` | Import from resume | ✅ Done | `POST /api/career/import-resume` (session required, rate-limited per tenant, 5 MB cap) takes a PDF, DOCX, plain text or a pasted body and returns a **draft**, never a write: `components/career/ResumeImport.tsx` shows every suggested field with the words it came from, the candidate ticks what to keep, and only then is it applied to the Career DNA form (still unsaved). Offered on `/app/career-dna` and inside onboarding step 2. The file is read in memory and discarded — nothing is stored. Extraction is dependency-free (`server/resume/extractText.ts`): a DOCX is a ZIP read through its central directory and inflated with `node:zlib`; a text PDF is its Flate streams' `Tj`/`TJ` operators, with escapes, octal codes and hex strings decoded and undecodable streams skipped rather than failing the file. A scanned PDF has no text at all, so `looksReadable()` gates the result and the route answers 422 with "paste it instead" rather than returning an empty profile. Parsing (`server/resume/parseResume.ts`) reuses the **same** `SKILL_LEXICON`, `extractSkills` and `inferSeniority` the product uses to read job postings — that shared vocabulary is what makes a skill found in a resume actually match a skill found in a posting. Skill strength follows how often a skill runs through the document; seniority reads only lines that look like held titles ("Reported to the director." is not a directorship); years prefers a stated "N years of experience" over the earliest dated role. Career goal, salary and work modes are deliberately never guessed. 30 unit tests, including PDFs and DOCXs built byte by byte in the tests themselves and the route's multipart, JSON, 415/422/400/401 paths. |
| `WJ-112` | Resume import rejected a normal, text-based PDF as "probably a scan" | ✅ Done | Reported with a real PDF and a screenshot proving it wasn't a scan. Root-caused two independent, pre-existing bugs in `server/resume/extractText.ts`'s hand-rolled PDF reader (no parsing dependency, by design): (1) the stream-scanner's `re.lastIndex = end` pointed at the *start* of `"endstream"`, not past it — since `"endstream"` itself contains the substring `"stream"`, the very next regex search re-matched inside it as a bogus new stream, corrupting detection of every stream after the first. Any PDF with more than one stream object — which is virtually all of them, since an embedded font and (when present) its `/ToUnicode` CMap are each their own stream — silently lost every stream after the first content stream. (2) No `/ToUnicode` CMap support at all: most real PDFs (Word, Google Docs, LaTeX, "Print to PDF") embed a subsetted font that gives each glyph an arbitrary internal code, recorded as the real character only in that font's own ToUnicode stream; without reading it, glyph codes decoded to unprintable control characters or the wrong letters, correctly failing `looksReadable` — a totally normal PDF came back indistinguishable from an actual scan. Fixed both at the root: the scanner now advances past `"endstream"` fully, and a `CMap` is built from every ToUnicode stream in the file (ToUnicode markers themselves used to identify and skip those streams as non-content) and threaded through both string forms a content stream can hold, tried first for 2-byte glyph codes and falling through to the prior heuristic when nothing resolves — safe for every existing plain-ASCII PDF, since an empty map changes nothing. A third bug surfaced while verifying against a real Chromium-rendered PDF: the embedded font *program* stream and any image stream are pure binary, not drawing operators, but their bytes could coincidentally match the Tj/TJ token pattern and inject garbage that diluted otherwise-perfectly-extracted prose below the readability threshold; both are now skipped up front (a font program's dict always carries `/Length1` per the PDF spec; an image's carries `/Subtype /Image` — neither a content nor a CMap stream ever does). Verified against two independently Chromium-generated PDFs (`page.pdf()`, real subsetted fonts, no synthetic fixtures involved) end to end through the actual `/app/career-dna` import UI in a real browser: both now read as `readable: true` with clean text, and `parseResume` correctly filled years of experience, skills, industries and location from the second. A residual, lower-severity cosmetic issue remains and is knowingly out of scope here: the content-stream reader treats every text-positioning operator as a line break, so a heading or word occasionally splits across lines when a real PDF renderer emits small positioning nudges mid-run (observed on "José García-Núñez" and "VP of Engineering" in the second test PDF) — it doesn't block readability or field extraction, both worked correctly despite it. 7 new unit tests, including one that pins the `endstream`-substring bug directly and one for the font-program/image pollution. `npm run check` 212/212. |
| `WJ-113` | Same "not a scan" error, on the user's own real CV — the "cosmetic" issue from WJ-112 was the actual bug | ✅ Done | The user supplied the actual failing file. It reproduced `readable: false` in isolation, output one character per line (`extractPdfText` returned "K\nu\nn\na\nl\n..."), which is exactly what WJ-112 flagged as a minor, out-of-scope cosmetic quirk — it wasn't minor, it was the whole bug for this common PDF-generation style. This résumé (an ATS-builder export) draws every *word* — the space between two words included — as its own `BT…ET` text object for exact kerning, and marks a real new line only by re-issuing the page's `cm` coordinate transform; it never uses a vertical `Td` at all. The reader's rule of "every `Td`/`TD`/`T*`/`ET` is a line break" is correct for some generators (a browser's own PDF export puts one whole line per `BT…ET`, confirmed by inspecting a real Chromium-generated PDF's content stream — 10 `BT` blocks for 10 lines) and catastrophically wrong for this one. Neither convention can be detected from the operator alone without tracking the real coordinate-transform stack, which this reader deliberately doesn't do (no parsing dependency, by design). Fixed with a heuristic that works for both real styles without that tracking: `T*` (the one operator the spec defines as an unconditional new line) and a matched `cm` invocation are treated as a hard line break — a `cm` is never observed mid-word, only at a real visual line/paragraph boundary; a new `BT` gets a plain space instead of a break, so a word-per-object generator doesn't run every word together; bare `Td`/`TD`/`ET` are no longer treated as line breaks at all. Two smaller bugs found alongside it: a synthetic space inserted before each `BT` combined with this generator's own drawn space-glyph to double every inter-word space — `tidy()` now collapses runs of 2+ literal spaces (safe and correct for any source); and `tidy()`'s space-stripping step had always been silently inert — its regex literal was a stray NUL byte (`/\0/g`) instead of a real space, invisibly typed in wrong at some point before this session and never once matching real text — removed as dead code rather than "fixed" into a working space-stripper, which would have deleted every space between every word in every PDF. Verified against the user's actual CV end to end through the real `/app/career-dna` import UI: `readable: true`, and the draft correctly filled name, headline, years of experience (9, from "earliest role starts 2017"), current level (Director), 14 matched skills and industries — also re-verified both earlier Chromium-generated test PDFs still extract cleanly, headings intact, no regressions. 3 new unit tests reproducing the word-per-`BT`/line-per-`cm` pattern directly. `npm run check` 215/215. |

### Testing

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-102` | Playwright E2E infrastructure + `auth.spec.ts` and `golden-journeys.spec.ts`, actually executed | 🟡 In progress | `apps/web/playwright.config.ts` + `apps/web/e2e/` stood up (`@playwright/test`, 5-project browser matrix, real Supabase backend — never mocked) and `auth.spec.ts` (18 tests) actually run against chromium: 13 passed, 5 honestly skipped, 0 failed, stable across repeated runs. Test accounts are created/deleted per test via the Supabase Admin API (`email_confirm: true`, never sends mail). Getting a real browser (not just CLI tools) through this sandbox's TLS-intercepting proxy needed `use.proxy` plus a static `--ignore-certificate-errors` launch flag (the per-connection `ignoreHTTPSErrors` context option wasn't enough — the proxy mints a fresh leaf cert per connection, which defeats Chromium's per-cert exception cache and produces `net::ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES`), both gated on `HTTPS_PROXY` so they no-op elsewhere. **Found and fixed a real product defect along the way:** `GET /demo` (`app/demo/route.ts`) unconditionally set the `wj_demo` cookie, which `proxy.ts` treats as authorization to skip the sign-in requirement on `/app`/`/onboarding`; Next.js's automatic `<Link>` prefetching (the marketing page's "Explore the demo" buttons use `Button`, which renders `next/link`) sends this exact request — tagged `next-router-prefetch: 1` — the moment the link scrolls into view, well before any click, silently flipping any landing-page visitor into demo mode. Surfaced because `AUTH-016` (protected routes reject access again after sign-out) genuinely failed: signing out lands on `/`, which renders those buttons, and the very next `/app` request wasn't redirected to sign-in. Fixed by skipping the cookie set when that header is present. Also fixed two test-authoring bugs found on first real execution: a `getByLabel("Password")` strict-mode violation (matched both the password field and the "Show password" toggle; needed `{ exact: true }`), and `AUTH-017`'s original draft using an unnamespaced localStorage key that never exercised the real per-tenant isolation logic (`` `${userId}:${name}` ``, `lib/mode.ts`) — rewritten to use the real key shape, which then correctly surfaced that `signOutEverywhere` clears the *signing-out account's own* local keys too (by design: local state is a cache, the server document is the source of truth on next sign-in), so `AUTH-007` was rewritten to assert the real, server-synced signal (onboarding-completion survives a sign-out/sign-in round trip for the same account) rather than a fabricated local marker. `AUTH-003` (real sign-up through the UI) is an honest, documented skip: this Supabase project has "Confirm email" on, and every domain tried either fails validation outright (`example.com`) or gets far enough to attempt a real send (confirmed via GoTrue's own rate limiter) — no domain exists that's both valid and guaranteed mail-free, so exercising it would violate the "never send real external email" rule. Firefox/WebKit/Mobile Safari confirmed BLOCKED by an actual launch attempt (no binaries in this sandbox), not assumed. `golden-journeys.spec.ts` (7 tests, entirely in demo mode — no real account needed, since demo mode auto-seeds a full job catalog, applications and Career DNA synchronously on boot and never gates behind onboarding) covers demo entry via a real click (not a prefetch, closing the loop on the bug above), the jobs list and a job's detail/match-explanation/save toggle, the "not for me" flow with a reason and undo, the applications dashboard's per-status routing (a submitted application opens its real timeline; a saved/preparing one instead opens the Prepare Application flow — confirmed both paths), and starting a Wonder run landing on that run's own timeline page. 7/7 passed, stable across a repeated run (14/14 on `--repeat-each=2`). Found two test-authoring bugs on first execution (both in the new spec's own assertions, not the product): a strict-mode selector collision between the sidebar's "Applications" link and the page's own back link, and a `waitForURL` target pattern that also matched the starting `/app/runs/new` URL itself (`"new"` satisfies `[^/]+` just like a real run id), so it resolved before the real navigation happened — fixed by excluding `"new"` explicitly. Full results, defects and fixes in `apps/web/docs/TEST_EXECUTION_REPORT.md`. **Remaining:** automation (scheduled runs, policy settings), Career DNA editing, BYOK/AI provider settings and PWA/push flows have no E2E coverage; golden journeys cover demo mode only, not a real signed-in account with genuine (non-seeded) data. |

### Extension

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-120` | A Chrome extension that fills an employer's application form with the materials WonderJobs prepared | ✅ Done | Asked for as "fill up job profiles directly on the actual job page with data from the curated WonderJobs section"; scope settled with the user: Greenhouse/Lever (plus a generic fallback), reuse the existing web session rather than a pasted key, and fill from the Career DNA base profile *and* the prepared materials for that specific posting. **Server:** `server/extensionToken.ts` mints a short-lived (30 min), HMAC-signed, read-only bearer token — the session cookie can't travel to an employer's origin, and a long-lived stored secret would be a worse trade; nothing is persisted server-side, so there is no token table to leak (6 unit tests incl. tamper, wrong-secret, expiry). `GET /api/extension/token` (cookie auth) mints it; `GET /api/extension/profile` and `GET /api/extension/application?url=` (bearer auth) serve the data, reading the tenant's own persisted stores through the existing `readClientState` seam the cron already uses. `services/jobs/atsUrl.ts` maps a real ATS page URL back to the `careers_…` job id — so the extension sends nothing but the URL and the server finds the matching application; a test pins it against `normalizePosting`'s own id for the same posting, including Greenhouse's newer `job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io` host and its embedded-form query shape (7 tests). The resume comes back as a real `.docx` (base64, reusing WJ-119's writer) and the cover letter as plain text via a new `markdownToPlainText`. **Extension (`extension/`, MV3, no build step, no dependencies):** a content script on WonderJobs' own origin mints the token and hands it to the service worker, which is the only thing that ever holds it or calls the API; the autofill content script matches Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby field names first, then falls back to reading each field's visible label, and attaches the resume to the file input via a `DataTransfer` (the only way to build a `FileList` from script). React-controlled inputs are written through the native value setter, since a plain `.value =` is ignored by React. An in-page panel reports exactly what was filled. **Honest by construction:** Career DNA holds no phone, LinkedIn or address, so those are never filled — the panel and the `/extension` page both say they're yours to type rather than inventing them, and a page with no matching application fills only the base profile and says so. Nothing is ever submitted. **Install entry points** (asked for separately): a landing-page `ExtensionSection`, a `/extension` page with honest "not on the Web Store yet, here's Load unpacked" steps serving `wonderjobs-extension.zip` (built by `npm run pack:extension`, a self-contained dependency-free zipper), a footer link, and — in the exact block the user pointed at — a line inside "Submit on \<company\>'s site" that offers the extension, or confirms it's already installed via a ping/pong handshake the bridge answers (`useExtensionInstalled`). **Verified for real, not asserted:** the unpacked extension was loaded into real Chromium (Playwright persistent context) against the live Groww Greenhouse posting — it minted a token against a running WonderJobs, matched the seeded application, filled First/Last name and attached `Groww-Resume.docx`, confirmed by Greenhouse's *own* uploader chip rendering the filename in the page's DOM (not ours), screenshotted. Email was correctly left blank there because the local session has no email address — exactly the designed behaviour. `npm run check` green (266/266, full production build). |

### Marketing

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WJ-121` | A shared link showed a title and description in WhatsApp but no logo | ✅ Done | Reported with a screenshot of two shared links rendering with no thumbnail. Root cause was not the image but the absence of one: the site declared **no `openGraph` metadata at all and no `metadataBase`**, so Next emitted only `<title>`/`<meta name=description>` — exactly what WhatsApp scraped. Added `app/opengraph-image.tsx` (the `next/og` + `brandMarkDataUri` pattern `icon.tsx`/`apple-icon.tsx` already use): a 1200×630 card with the butterfly mark and wordmark, flat colours on purpose since WhatsApp silently drops a preview image over a few hundred KB — this renders at 96 KB. `lib/siteUrl.ts` resolves the absolute origin (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` → `VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL`, which Vercel sets even on previews → `VERCEL_URL` → localhost) and feeds `metadataBase`, without which Next emits *relative* og:image URLs that no scraper can fetch. `title`/`description` are deliberately **not** pinned inside the root `openGraph`: leaving them out is what lets each page's own title flow into og:title, so `/extension` shares as "Browser extension · WonderJobs" rather than the brand line. A shared *job* link redirects to `/sign-in?next=…`, so that page's tags are what gets shown — it now has a `generateMetadata` that reuses `publicJobTeaser` to name the real role ("Senior Staff Software Engineer, Platform - IAM · Coinbase") instead of "Sign in". Two real bugs were caught by checking the output rather than assuming: (1) the description rendered `undefined` because `WORK_MODE_LABEL` was imported from `components/jobs/JobCard.tsx`, a `"use client"` module — on the server that resolves to a client *reference*, not the object, so the lookup silently returned undefined; moved the constant to `domain/jobs/types.ts` (where the other five importers now read it) and the footgun is gone. (2) Returning an `openGraph` object from the sign-in route *replaced* the inherited one and took the file-convention image with it, leaving the very link being shared with no logo again — fixed by returning only `title`/`description` and letting them flow. Verified by fetching each page with a WhatsApp user agent and reading the emitted tags: og:image absolute, 1200×630, `summary_large_image`, present on the landing page, `/extension` and the shared-job sign-in URL. `npm run check` green (266/266, full production build). |

The owner adds collaborators (any creator they can see who hasn't blocked them) with a part (e.g. Co-writer) and access: comment, propose changes, or edit; collaborators can leave. Proposals are made on the current version and reviewed as a line diff against the current text; the owner accepts (a new version credited to the proposer, "Proposed by …") or declines with an optional note; proposers can withdraw. Conflicts are explicit: a proposal on an older version is flagged "Piece changed since" and can only be accepted after the owner confirms they compared it; a direct edit on a stale base is refused with the text kept in the editor. Edit access saves new versions credited to the editor. Comments (optionally on a quoted passage and version) are visible to the owner and collaborators; the owner or author resolves them. "Who wrote what" lists every version by person (AI marked as AI, restores marked) — contributions are never flattened. ### Compliance & platform hardening

| ID | Story | Status | Notes |

| `C-1` | C-1 Security hardening | ✅ Done | Password policy (10+, letters and digits, common-list, no email) in browser and server; password reset; change password with step-up; TOTP two-step verification (sign-in gate, API 401 until verified); Fetch Metadata CSRF refusal; COOP/CORP/Origin-Agent-Cluster headers; audit-log integrity (reserved server-only namespaces, via: session stamp, no truncate); CI: CodeQL, gitleaks, npm audit, Dependabot; security.txt and /legal/security |
| `C-2` | C-2 Privacy (GDPR / DPDP) | ✅ Done | Versioned notice; per-purpose, append-only consent records with proof (version, method, time); required consents gate every signed-in page and are re-asked when the notice changes; optional usage measures and emails off by default and withdrawable in Settings (telemetry honours it); 18+ declaration; data-principal requests (access, correction, erasure, portability, objection, consent withdrawal, nomination, grievance) with 30-day due dates and server-written audit; complete export checked against the schema by a DB test; daily retention purge; public Privacy notice, Terms and Subprocessors; RoPA, retention schedule and breach runbook in docs/compliance/privacy.md. Owner: entity details, Grievance Officer, DPAs, counsel review |
| `C-3` | C-3 Payments (Stripe / Razorpay) | ✅ Done | Done (provider-gated) — @wonder/creator-payments: Razorpay Payment Links for INR, Stripe Checkout otherwise (REST, hosted pages, SAQ-A). Orders opened from the licence (amount never from the client; one live order per licence), provider references recorded server-side, signed webhooks (Stripe timestamped HMAC, Razorpay HMAC) applied once per event id with amount/currency checks and double-settlement guard; balanced, append-only double-entry ledger; licence income in Business settles automatically; payee refunds with password, confirmed by webhook (dashboard refunds recorded too). UI: Pay / Copy payment link / Refund on the licence, a return page that waits for confirmation, provider status in Settings. Owner: keys, webhooks, merchant-of-record decision (docs/compliance/payments.md) |
| `C-4` | C-4 Financial controls (SOX-style) | ✅ Done | Controls matrix (docs/compliance/financial-controls.md): settled records locked against creator edits; daily reconciliation (journals balance, order vs ledger, paid order ↔ business record, unapplied provider events, unconfirmed refunds, stale checkouts expired) with immutable exceptions and an audited run; creator payment statement (CSV, injection-safe, audited); financial records excluded from retention; CODEOWNERS on money/privacy/security/schema paths. Owner: branch protection, control owners, sign-offs |
| `C-5` | C-5 Landing page | ✅ Done | Public / for signed-out visitors (proxy rewrite to /welcome; signed-in creators keep Home): painted arches hero, Tagline, "Create your studio"; highlight chips; four trust pillars — Stripe & Razorpay, GDPR & DPDP, SOX-style controls, security by default — each describing only what ships, with links to the legal pages and a no-certification note.
